$schema_intent: AI-targeted structured defect log for the devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1 feature. Each entry is self-contained so an AI agent loading a single record has every fact it needs to reproduce, diagnose, and fix the defect without re-reading the whole codebase. Human-readable narrative lives in the sibling .md files; this file is the canonical machine-actionable surface.

live_reproduction_environment.all_5_oss_local_install_commands_attempt: T1.1 install pass at 2026-05-24T02:29-02:33Z; results captured in .claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl

scan_metadata.live_mcp_server_connection_count: 2 of 7 actually reachable (terraform-mcp + actionlint-mcp); 5 misconfigured at config or transport layer

defects.title: Probe script reads `.transport` field but `.mcp.json` schema uses `.type`

evidence.spec_citation: Claude Code docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp-servers.md): .mcp.json HTTP server entries declare `"type": "http"` (alias `streamable-http`). There is no `transport` field in .mcp.json — `transport` is a CLI-only `claude mcp add --transport http` flag.
observable_in_jsonl: .claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl line 6: {"server":"context7","result":"fail","failure_layer":"config","latency_ms":28,"message_redacted":"stdio entry has no command field"}
evidence.reproduction_command: jq -r '.mcpServers.context7 | if .transport == "http" then "http" else "stdio" end' /workspaces/feature-pipeline/.mcp.json # → prints 'stdio' (WRONG); replace .transport with .type → prints 'http' (CORRECT)

defects.root_cause: The mcp-ping.sh author confused two different Claude Code surfaces: the .mcp.json schema (which uses `type`) and the `claude mcp add` CLI flag (which uses `--transport`). The two are not synonyms. The probe is the ONLY consumer of .mcp.json in the lifecycle scripts, so the mismatch had no compile-time signal.
defects.impact: All HTTP MCP servers (context7, exa) are misrouted to `probe_stdio()`, which then reads .command, finds none, and emits 'stdio entry has no command field'. The probe latency of 28-30ms (vs the 10s stdio-timeout used for genuinely-unreachable servers) is the smoking gun. Claude Code itself reads .type correctly and these servers connect fine when actually used.

fix.verification_command: echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' | timeout 5 curl -sS -H "x-api-key: $EXA_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -X POST -d @- https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp

defects.title: Probe script omits MCP `initialize` handshake before calling `tools/list`

evidence.spec_citation: MCP specification 2025-11-25 §lifecycle: 'The client SHOULD NOT send requests other than pings before the server has responded to the initialize request.' Servers MAY reject such calls. Canonical three-message sequence: (1) client → initialize request, (2) server → initialize response, (3) client → notifications/initialized.
observable_in_jsonl: .claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl line 8: {"server":"actionlint-mcp","status":"degraded","error":"method \"tools/list\" is invalid during session initialization"} — server enforced the spec
.claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl lines 11-13: gitnexus / mcp-openapi-schema / serena all timed out at 10s waiting for an initialize that never came
evidence.live_reproduction_strict_server: echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' | actionlint-mcp # → returns JSON-RPC error: method invalid during session initialization
evidence.live_reproduction_correct_handshake:
printf '%s
%s
%s
' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"probe","version":"0.0.1"}}}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' | actionlint-mcp # → returns serverInfo + full tool catalog in <1s

defects.root_cause: The probe author assumed MCP servers would accept tools/list before the session was established. The MCP spec rejects this. Implementations split into two failure modes: strict servers (actionlint-mcp) reject with a JSON-RPC error; lenient servers (gitnexus) wait for the missing initialize and time out at the 10s wrapper limit.
defects.impact: All 4 stdio servers register as 'degraded' or 'unreachable' in mcp-events.jsonl even when they are perfectly functional. Operators see false alarms and may chase phantom install issues (as happened in this case).

fix.edit_strategy: Rewrite probe_stdio() to send the three-message sequence and parse the SECOND response (the tools/list response, since the FIRST is the initialize response). OR adopt the cheaper alternative: send only `initialize` and treat parseable `result.serverInfo` as success — this avoids the `head -1` race against the unrelated stderr/notification timing.
fix.secondary_fix_note: Replace `head -1` with reading until JSON-RPC id=1 appears, since some servers (gitnexus) emit pino log lines to stdout before the response.

defects.title: `.mcp.json` invokes mcp-openapi-schema with no schema-path argument and no openapi.yaml exists in repo

evidence.server_help_output:
Usage: node index.mjs [path/to/openapi.yaml]
Arguments:
  path/to/openapi.yaml  Path to the OpenAPI schema file (JSON or YAML) (optional)
                       If not provided, defaults to openapi.yaml
evidence.server_source_behavior: Reads process.argv[2]; if absent, resolves './openapi.yaml' against process.cwd(); if file missing, logs ENOENT and exits non-zero before any MCP handshake response.
evidence.live_reproduction: mcp-openapi-schema # → 'Error loading schema: Error opening file "/workspaces/feature-pipeline/openapi.yaml" ENOENT: no such file or directory'
evidence.adr_prescription_violated: ADR-0041 §Decision Details install-mechanism taxonomy explicitly defines this invocation form: `npx -y "mcp-openapi-schema@${MCP_OPENAPI_SCHEMA_VERSION}" <spec-path>` (with `<spec-path>` token). The implementation dropped the `<spec-path>` token without recording why.

defects.root_cause: Two compounding failures: (a) the .mcp.json author did not pass an argv path or place an openapi.yaml at repo root; (b) the ADR-0041 taxonomy that prescribed `<spec-path>` was not enforced by any audit check. The package is also abandoned upstream (single 2025-03-13 release per npm; single 'Initial commit' on hannesj/mcp-openapi-schema; 6 open issues, no subsequent commits) and was already flagged in versions.env as `STALE_PACKAGE per H-3`.
defects.impact: The server self-terminates within milliseconds of being launched, so Claude Code's MCP loader will register it as failed-to-start. The 'install_complete' record at JSONL line 2 was correct (the npm package installed); only the runtime invocation is broken. Even after fixing DEF-02 (probe handshake), this server would still fail because it dies before responding.

fix.option_a_minimal: Decide which OpenAPI spec is the target, place it at a known path, and update args: `"args": ["-y", "mcp-openapi-schema@${MCP_OPENAPI_SCHEMA_VERSION}", "${workspaceFolder}/openapi.yaml"]` (or absolute path).
fix.option_b_remove: If no target OpenAPI spec exists in the repo (current state), remove the server entry from .mcp.json AND remove `mcp__mcp-openapi-schema__*` from the design-api agent allowlist. design-api currently relies on this MCP for no purpose; the spec it would consume does not exist.
fix.option_c_replace: Swap to `mcp-openapi-schema-explorer` (kadykov, actively maintained, last pushed 2026-05-18, supports HTTP(S) URLs as well as local paths). Same surface area; different package id. Requires updating .mcp.json server name AND the per-agent allowlist token.
fix.recommended: option_b_remove until an OpenAPI spec is actually checked in; option_c_replace if the design-api consumer is load-bearing.

defects.title: `.mcp.json` invokes serena via `uvx` but uv/uvx is not installed in the devcontainer image

evidence.binary_check: command -v uvx # → (no output); find / -name uvx -type f 2>/dev/null # → no results
evidence.dockerfile_evidence: /workspaces/feature-pipeline/.devcontainer/Dockerfile installs only ripgrep/jq/bat/tree/less via apt; no uv install.
evidence.devcontainer_features_evidence: .devcontainer/devcontainer.json declares features: common-utils, github-cli, node:1@20, go:1@1.22, anthropics/claude-code:1. NO uv feature, no python-tools-with-uv feature.
evidence.install_log_evidence: .claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl line 1: {"event":"install_complete","server":"serena","status":"failed","note":"uvx serena --version failed"} — postCreate.sh:61 attempted `uvx --from ... serena --version` and got 'No such file or directory' on uvx itself.
evidence.live_reproduction: uvx --from git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@v1.2.0 serena --version # → 'timeout: failed to run command \u2018uvx\u2019: No such file or directory'

defects.root_cause: ADR-0041's install-taxonomy table treats `uvx` as if it is automatically available, but uv/uvx is not installed by any Dockerfile RUN or devcontainer feature in this project. The base image (mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:1-3.11-bookworm) ships pip but not uv. The Node and Go features were added; uv was overlooked.
defects.secondary_concern: Per upstream Serena README (github.com/oraios/serena): the project explicitly warns 'Do not install Serena via an MCP or plugin marketplace! They contain outdated and suboptimal installation commands.' The canonical install is `uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent@latest --prerelease=allow` (PyPI package `serena-agent`), not `uvx --from git+...@<ref>`. The ADR-0041 git-ref invocation is non-canonical AND the implementation is missing the upstream-prescribed `start-mcp-server` argv (see DEF-05).
defects.impact: Serena never starts. The install fails at postCreate (so no sentinel exists), then every subsequent postStart probe times out. Five separate places reference SERENA_REF: devcontainer.json containerEnv, versions.env, .mcp.json args, postCreate.sh install_serena(), and .install-sentinel-serena-${SERENA_REF} naming. All carry a v1.2.0 pin against an install path that cannot execute.

fix.step_1_install_uv: Add to .devcontainer/Dockerfile (preferred — image-time, cached): `RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh && ln -sf /home/vscode/.local/bin/uv /usr/local/bin/uv && ln -sf /home/vscode/.local/bin/uvx /usr/local/bin/uvx` (adjust the path to wherever the installer drops the binaries for the user). Alternative: use a third-party devcontainer feature such as `ghcr.io/va-h/devcontainers-features/uv:1` in devcontainer.json features.
fix.step_2_decide_invocation: Either keep the git-ref form and add `serena start-mcp-server` to args (matches DEF-05 fix), OR switch to the upstream-canonical `uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent` flow in postCreate.sh and call `serena start-mcp-server` directly from .mcp.json (no uvx).
fix.step_3_reconsider_pin: ADR-0040 pinned pre-v1.3.0 (last known: v1.2.0). Current upstream is v1.5.1 (2026-05-18). The base_modes→added_modes review that justified the pin must either complete or be re-deferred explicitly; the pin should not silently drift further out of date.

defects.title: `.mcp.json` serena invocation omits the `start-mcp-server` argv prescribed by ADR-0041

evidence.adr_prescription_text: Serena | uvx --from (Python; uv-managed; ephemeral) | uvx --from "git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@${SERENA_REF}" serena start-mcp-server
evidence.postcreate_smoke_form: postCreate.sh:61 runs `uvx --from ... serena --version` for smoke-testing — that's a different invocation than the runtime-launch form. The smoke form does not exercise the missing argv.

defects.root_cause: Two-form discipline gap: the install-smoke-test command and the runtime-launch command differ, and the ADR-prescribed runtime form was not copied verbatim into .mcp.json. The discrepancy survived the audit because no auditor compares .mcp.json args against the ADR-0041 taxonomy table.
defects.impact: Compounds DEF-04: even if uvx were installed, calling `serena` (without `start-mcp-server`) would invoke serena's CLI help/dispatcher, not launch the MCP stdio loop. The server would never become reachable.

fix.audit_addition_needed: Add an OP rule comparing .mcp.json invocation strings against the ADR-0041 install-taxonomy table for each named server. This is a config-vs-design-contract check; currently no auditor performs it.

defects.title: Sentinel file location and naming diverge from ADR-0041 §Decision §2
affects_servers: all 5 OSS-local installs (serena, mcp-openapi-schema, actionlint-mcp, terraform-mcp, gitnexus)

evidence.adr_self_assertion: The unversioned form in the postCreate.sh outline is the bug; the version-pinned form is the canonical convention.
evidence.implementation_actual_naming: postCreate.sh line 52/78/102/135: `.install-sentinel-<server>-<version>` (dot-prefixed, dashes not @-separators, no `.installed` suffix)
evidence.filesystem_evidence: ls /workspaces/feature-pipeline/.claude/runtime/install-sentinels/ # → No such file or directory. Actual files at .claude/runtime/.install-sentinel-actionlint-mcp-7441fe042c995cbb1bb4b97fce71f9ed3b36d5ef etc.

defects.root_cause: The same author that wrote postCreate.sh did not consult ADR-0041 §Decision §2 (or consulted a draft that predated the I-DR-CS-001 resolution). The ADR explicitly resolved this exact inconsistency in favor of the version-pinned form under install-sentinels/, then the implementation ignored the resolution.
defects.impact: Pure behavior is unaffected (any naming works as long as it's internally consistent), but the violation breaks any tooling that consumes the ADR-prescribed sentinel layout, and it signals weak ADR-to-code discipline that lowers confidence in every other ADR claim.

fix.migration: Existing sentinel files will not match the new pattern — postCreate will treat installs as missing and re-run (idempotent; safe). Consider a one-line migration in postCreate.sh that mv's any legacy `.install-sentinel-*` files to the new path before the existence checks.

defects.title: discovery-external-researcher agent allowlists exa tool names that the live exa MCP no longer exposes

evidence.live_tool_surface_observed_2026_05_24: Deferred-tool listing in active session declares exa exposes: mcp__exa__web_fetch_exa, mcp__exa__web_search_exa. The two tools the allowlist names (company_research_exa, crawling_exa) are absent.
evidence.side_effect: When the agent calls mcp__exa__crawling_exa, Claude Code returns 'tool not exposed by server' rather than executing the call. The web_search_exa entry still works.

defects.root_cause: Exa's hosted MCP product evolved (likely renamed tools) and the agent allowlist was never refreshed. There is no automated check that the named `mcp__<server>__<tool>` entries in agent allowlists actually exist on the live server.
defects.impact: Two of three exa tool entries in the allowlist are silently dead. Agents that need crawling or company-research capability via exa will fail at tool-call time, not at config-load time. This is a soft-fail mode that masks misconfiguration.

fix.step_1_refresh: Run a live tools/list against https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp using the canonical 3-message handshake; record the returned tool names; update discovery-external-researcher.md allowlist to exactly that set.
fix.step_2_audit_rule: Add an auditing-mcp OP rule that (when --with-runtime is genuinely runtime) probes each HTTP server's tools/list and diff's against the per-agent `mcp__<server>__<tool>` allowlists. This is the only way to catch upstream tool-surface drift.

defects.title: `audit_mcp.py --with-runtime` is misnamed — it performs no live MCP-server probe of the registered servers

evidence.runtime_flag_handling: audit_mcp.py lines 36, 56-58: parses --with-runtime, passes it through ONLY to check_toxic_combinations.py. validate_mcp_config.py, scan_mcp_secrets.py, and OP-1..OP-10 do not receive the flag.
evidence.toxic_combinations_runtime_behavior: check_toxic_combinations.py --with-runtime spawns each server and queries tools/list to categorize them — but does so for toxic-combination detection (filesystem+web, etc.), NOT for verifying that THIS project's 7 registered servers are reachable, return their expected tool surface, or match per-agent allowlists.
evidence.gate_6_dependency: PV-5.C-HARDGATE per phase-validators.md: 'python audit_mcp.py --with-runtime --severity-threshold BLOCKER exits 0; the produced report shows 0 BLOCKER findings across OP-1..OP-10'. The gate trusts a static analysis disguised as a runtime check.
evidence.consequence_observed: audit_mcp.py against current state returns exit 0 with 0 BLOCKER, even though 5 of 7 servers are demonstrably broken (DEF-01..DEF-04). The hard gate let the broken artifacts through.

defects.root_cause: The name `--with-runtime` was attached to a flag that only enables toxic-combination probing, not end-to-end MCP-server reachability verification. PV-5 was authored as if `--with-runtime` would perform the latter; the implementation only does the former.
defects.impact: The PV-5 hard gate — described in ADR-0043 as 'MCPs can cause a lot of problems if they are not stable and the system fails silently' — does not actually verify that any of the 7 servers can be started, do a handshake, and expose the tools the per-agent allowlists name. The gate is a paper tiger against exactly the failure class it was created to prevent.

fix.design_change: Rename `--with-runtime` to `--with-toxic-runtime` and add a new `--with-mcp-reachability` flag (or a unified `--live`) that: (1) launches each .mcp.json server using the exact command+args+env that Claude Code would; (2) performs the 3-message MCP handshake; (3) records the tools/list response; (4) diffs the tool set against per-agent allowlists; (5) emits BLOCKER findings on handshake failure or tool-not-found.
fix.audit_addition_needed: Plug the new live-reachability script into audit_mcp.py. The PV-5 contract must require BOTH static OP-1..OP-10 AND the live reachability check. No exit 0 unless all 7 servers respond.

defects.title: Feature shipped `delivery_status: ready-for-execution-validation` without ever performing PV-5 live verification

evidence.verify_at_execution_t5_2: verify-at-execution.md §T5.2: 'Status: rebuild-dependent; CANNOT be executed from the parent orchestrator session without disrupting the user's active Codespace. Documented as user-driven exercise per Phase 5 T5.2 contract.'
evidence.execution_state_log_evidence: state-transitions.log records execution pipeline T0 at 2026-05-23T03:20:00Z, T5 (escalated_stub) at 2026-05-23T18:20:00Z after only 4/10 Phase-0 tasks (T0.1, T0.3 PASS; T0.2, T0.4 SURFACED FINDINGS; T0.5..T0.10 NOT EXECUTED). Phases 1-5 of the execution pipeline never ran.
evidence.git_log_evidence: Commits 6f46d14 and 094d47e ('feat: devcontainer-mcp-provisioning-r1 Phase 5 — rollout + hard-gate exercise', etc.) record that the code was eventually committed — but the execution pipeline that should have driven those commits never ran past Phase 0.
evidence.phase_validator_evidence: phase-validators.md PV-5.C1..C21 (BLOCKER each) include 'Fresh Codespace cold-cache rebuild' (C1), 'claude mcp list returns 7 connected entries' (C4), 'AC-X-1 failure-mode rehearsal: missing env-var produces distinguishable failure' (C8). NONE of these were executed against a fresh Codespace.
evidence.audit_run_only_static: T5.4 audit ran audit_mcp.py against repo files only — a STATIC check. The PV-5 hard gate was satisfied by the static check returning exit 0; the live C1..C21 checks were deferred to 'user-driven' status with no enforcement.

defects.root_cause: Two compounding gaps: (a) the phase validator framework treats live-environment checks as 'specified but executable later by humans'; the orchestrator has no machinery to drive a fresh Codespace rebuild and observe the results; (b) the deliverable packager accepted `delivery_status: ready-for-execution-validation` as a valid shippable state. The pipeline shipped a feature whose acceptance tests were specified-but-not-run.
defects.impact: Every defect DEF-01..DEF-07 is a direct consequence of this gap. If PV-5.C4 had been mechanically enforced ('claude mcp list returns 7 connected entries'), the pipeline would have halted on this very feature. Instead the static audit ran, returned green, and the broken artifacts shipped.

fix.principle: PV-5 hard-gate criteria that require a live environment must EITHER (a) be executable by the orchestrator (e.g., the orchestrator can rebuild and verify, treating the long wall-clock cost as a gate cost), OR (b) be downgraded to non-BLOCKER and ineligible to gate-pass the feature. The current 'specified-but-deferred-to-user' middle ground is the worst of both: it labels itself BLOCKER while having no enforcement.
fix.concrete_change_1: Add a `tests/postship-smoke.sh` script that runs in a CI container (or a recyclable Codespace) and exercises the live PV-5.C1..C21 sequence. The feature pipeline blocks on this script's exit code at Gate 6.
fix.concrete_change_2: Forbid the deliverable packager from emitting `approved` (or any green status) for FULL-scope features when verify-at-execution.md contains any §T5.x section in 'user-driven; not executed' state.

defects.title: Architecture audit verdict was `approved_with_conditions` despite known design-vs-implementation drift

evidence.audit_scope_evidence: The audit surfaced I-AA-001 (filename drift design-cc vs design-claude-code) and I-AA-002 (consumer-set math narrative). It did NOT compare ADR-0041 install-taxonomy strings against .mcp.json invocations, did NOT verify uvx availability, did NOT verify sentinel location matches ADR-0041 §Decision §2.
evidence.audit_dimensions_evidence: The architecture-audit dimensions covered claim-verification, brief-honor, blast-radius — none of which exercise 'does the prescribed install path actually exist at runtime?' or 'does .mcp.json match the ADR taxonomy?'

defects.root_cause: The architecture audit dimensions focus on internal-consistency of design artifacts and against synthesis claims. They do not include a 'design-vs-codebase-reality' axis. ADR-0041 was internally consistent; the codebase implementation drifted from ADR-0041; the audit had no rule that fired on the gap.
defects.impact: The Gate-4 approval relied on this audit. The drift discovered here (DEF-05, DEF-06, plus the underlying DEF-04 prerequisite gap) was already latent at the audit moment and was not flagged.

fix.audit_dimension_addition: Add a 'design-realization-check' axis to review-architecture-auditor: for every ADR that names a concrete file/command/path/argv, verify the named artifact exists in the codebase and matches the ADR specification verbatim. Treat divergence as a MAJOR finding minimum.

defects.title: Cross-artifact audit cycle 4 verdict `needs_reconciliation` with `count: 0` — pipeline ignored a non-pass verdict

evidence.deliverable_archive_status: Listed cycle 4 as 'converged' in the artifact index notes; delivery_status: ready-for-execution-validation

defects.root_cause: Either the auditor emitted an inconsistent verdict (needs_reconciliation with no findings is structurally invalid — there's nothing to reconcile) OR the downstream consumer of the verdict treated 'no findings' as 'converged' regardless of the .verdict string. Either way, the pipeline accepted a non-PASS as PASS.
defects.impact: The 4-cycle reconciliation cap was 'used up' on this cycle without delivering a definitive verdict, and the orchestrator moved forward as if the verdict were green. Any future audit run that produces this structure will quietly pass.

fix.rule: Reconciler logic must treat any .verdict != 'pass' as a hard halt regardless of findings count. If 'needs_reconciliation' is emitted with 0 findings, the auditor itself is broken — surface this as an orchestrator-level error, not a pass.
fix.audit_writer_invariant: test-acceptance-author + review-cross-artifact-auditor should never emit verdict==needs_reconciliation with findings==0. Add this as a frontmatter-validation rule in the reviewer.

defects.title: Execution pipeline ran in 'single-agent-fallback' mode — quality handlers and phase reviewers never invoked

evidence.state_transitions_log: state-transitions.log T0-prime entry: 'corrective_action: re-enter pending; dispatch Phase-0 parallel leaves T0.1..T0.10' and context.single-agent-fallback note from checkpoint.json: 'single-agent-fallback mode elected (brief option c)'.
evidence.checkpoint_log: checkpoint.json T0-prime: trigger='re-invocation after false-blocker void; single-agent-fallback mode elected (brief option c)'
evidence.missing_quality_dispatch: No Task() calls to execute-task-quality-handler or execute-phase-quality-reviewer recorded in state-transitions.log. The Per-Task Quality Verdict step (T2) and Phase Quality Review (T7) never executed; the orchestrator did the code-producer work itself and self-graded.
evidence.per_task_results: Only two per-task-execution-result.json records exist: T2.3 (SKILL.md edit) and T4.1 (template edit). 37 of 39 tasks have no execution result artifact at all.

defects.root_cause: The execute-orchestrator initially reported a missing-dispatch-tool blocker, was voided by a user corrective brief, and resumed in 'single-agent-fallback' mode — but this mode bypasses the verdict-issuer separation that the pipeline's defense-in-depth depends on. The single agent now both produces code and grades it; there is no independent quality verdict.
defects.impact: Every defect in DEF-01..DEF-07 was either authored or accepted by the same agent. The execute-task-quality-handler's detect_stubs.py + 4-phase verification, and execute-phase-quality-reviewer's dimensional verdict, never ran on this feature's execution artifacts.

fix.principle: Single-agent-fallback must NOT be a valid mode for FULL-scope features when the deliverable acceptance depends on multi-agent quality enforcement. The fallback was authored as an emergency continuation path; using it on the canonical happy path defeats the pipeline's purpose.
fix.concrete_change: When the orchestrator detects it cannot dispatch the verdict-issuer subagents, the recipe must HALT and require user re-invocation with the correct tool grants — not fall back to single-agent mode.

summary_for_ai_consumers.pipeline_phase_at_which_actual_code_was_: single-agent-fallback after Phase-0 escalation — not via the execute-task-code-producer / execute-task-quality-handler / execute-phase-quality-reviewer dispatch chain
summary_for_ai_consumers.primary_failure_mode: The pipeline's hard gate (PV-5.C-HARDGATE per ADR-0043) trusted a static analysis disguised as a runtime check. None of the 7 servers were ever launched-and-verified by the gate.
summary_for_ai_consumers.secondary_failure_mode: Even within static analysis, the auditors had no rule that compared .mcp.json invocation strings against ADR-0041's install-taxonomy table. ADR-vs-implementation drift was therefore invisible to the audits.
